prompts.title: Recent Form — Wins, Draws and Losses
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 frame, about 8 seconds, timed to the spoken beat. Reserve the lower quarter as a permanent subtitle band: charcoal #101412 scrim with warm white #edf0e6 Spanish captions, and no graphic element may enter that zone. Background is GoatLab charcoal #101412 with a faint slate #8ca6bf grain. Editorial variant — kinetic typography with rhythmic emphasis. Open on the Spanish word FORMA in a condensed heavy warm white face, centred just above the subtitle band. On each percussive beat one result token stamps in: VICTORIA in lime #c5ed74, EMPATE in warm white, DERROTA in slate #8ca6bf, each snapping with a two-frame overshoot and a thin lime underline. Tokens stack into two columns, Chelsea FC left and AFC Bournemouth right, separated by a vertical slate hairline. A lime halo pulse sweeps down the Chelsea column, then the Bournemouth column, syncing to the voice. No axes, no numerals, no invented match events. Camera drifts slowly upward. Transition into the statistical variant is a horizontal wipe from centre outward, then the columns fade. Statistical variant — grouped count bars. Chart type: grouped vertical bars, three per team ordered victorias, empates, derrotas, all standing on a shared zero baseline with one common scale covering both teams so the tallest bar tops the plotting area. Chelsea bars lime #c5ed74, Bournemouth bars slate #8ca6bf, with warm white value numerals resolved from {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}}, {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}} and {{away.losses}}. Spanish axis title: Partidos · últimos encuentros; unit label partidos. Sample annotation sits under each team name as muestra: {{home.n}} and muestra: {{away.n}}, with provider credited as source Bzzoiro. A small badge compares the two and reads muestras no equivalentes only when they differ. Entry: bars grow from the baseline in staggered order, Chelsea first. Emphasis: the largest bar lifts its numeral with a lime glow while the others dim for a beat. Camera pushes from full frame to a five-sixths crop centred on the bars. Exit: bars retract to the baseline, the Spanish axis title holds briefly, then the frame dissolves to charcoal.

prompts.title: Goals For and Against — Paired Bars
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 frame, about 8 seconds, locked to the spoken line. The lower quarter is a permanent subtitle band with a charcoal #101412 scrim and warm white #edf0e6 Spanish captions; keep graphics out of it. Editorial variant — illustrative football pitch and ball path. A top-down pitch drawn in thin slate #8ca6bf lines on GoatLab charcoal #101412 fills the upper three quarters; the halfway line separates Chelsea FC on the left, accented in lime #c5ed74, from AFC Bournemouth on the right, accented in slate. Two generic flat monogram shields, no real badges, sit on the centre circle. A warm white ball travels a curved path from the left third toward the right goal trailing a lime ribbon; on each beat the ribbon thickens, then a second slate ribbon returns right to left. The ribbons converge into two opposing arrows that halt beneath the Spanish heading GOLES. No numerals, no axes, no invented match events. Camera is a slow orbit of about twenty degrees around the pitch centre. Transition into the statistical variant: the pitch lines retract into one horizontal rule that becomes the chart axis. Statistical variant — paired bars. Chart type: two paired vertical bars per team, one for Goles a favor and one for Goles en contra, grouped side by side on a shared zero baseline with one common scale so all four bars are directly comparable. Spanish unit label: goles · últimos encuentros. Values resolved from {{home.gf}}, {{home.ga}}, {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}}. Favour bars use lime #c5ed74; against bars use slate #8ca6bf with a diagonal hatch so the pairing reads instantly. Team headers Chelsea FC and AFC Bournemouth in warm white above each pair. Beneath them the sample annotation in Spanish: muestra: {{home.n}} partidos and muestra: {{away.n}} partidos, with source credit Bzzoiro in small warm white type at the foot of the plotting area. Entry: the four bars rise from the baseline in one sweep while numerals count up. Emphasis: a lime outline pulses around the pair with the taller favour bar, dimming the opposite pair for a beat. Camera pushes to a five-sixths crop on the numerals, then pulls back. Exit: bars fold flat onto the baseline and the frame dissolves to charcoal.

prompts.title: Clean Sheets — Counts and Sample Sizes
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 frame, about 7 seconds. Permanent lower-quarter subtitle band: charcoal #101412 scrim with warm white #edf0e6 Spanish captions; the design field is everything above it. Editorial variant — defensive energy and a stylised shield. A large flat shield outline in lime #c5ed74 sits centre-frame on GoatLab charcoal #101412, drawn as one continuous stroke that animates as if being forged: entering at the top edge, sweeping down the left flank, closing at the point. Inside the shield the Spanish word SÓLIDO breathes slowly in condensed warm white capitals. Two narrower shields flank it, left labelled Chelsea FC in lime, right labelled AFC Bournemouth in slate #8ca6bf. Slate energy streaks ricochet off the shield faces on each percussive beat and disperse into fine particles. No numerals, no axes, no invented saves or match events. Camera holds a locked frame, then tilts up slightly on the final beat. Transition into the statistical variant: the central shield splits vertically into two halves that slide apart, opening a clean charcoal panel for the chart. Statistical variant — counts only, never rates. Chart type: two vertical count columns on a shared zero baseline with one common scale, Spanish title Arcos en cero and unit label partidos. Left column lime #c5ed74 labelled Chelsea FC, right column slate #8ca6bf labelled AFC Bournemouth. Heights and numerals resolved from {{home.clean}} and {{away.clean}}. Directly beneath each column a sample annotation in Spanish: muestra: {{home.n}} partidos and muestra: {{away.n}} partidos, plus the small line recuento, no tasa so no viewer reads the bars as a rate. Source credit Bzzoiro appears in small warm white type at the foot of the plotting area. Entry: columns grow from the baseline in sequence, Chelsea first. Emphasis: a thin lime bracket frames the gap between the two column tops, drawing the eye to the difference without commentary, while both numerals hold steady. Camera settles into a slow push from full frame to a five-sixths crop. Exit: the bracket closes, both columns retract to the baseline, the two shield halves slide back together, and the frame fades to charcoal.

prompts.title: Head-to-Head — Historical Meeting Split
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 frame, about 9 seconds. Reserve the lower quarter for the permanent Spanish subtitle band, charcoal #101412 scrim beneath warm white #edf0e6 captions. Editorial variant — both teams presented as a visual duel. The frame splits on a slightly tilted diagonal: Chelsea FC territory left in deep charcoal with a lime #c5ed74 edge light, AFC Bournemouth territory right with a slate #8ca6bf edge light. Two flat monogram blocks advance from opposite edges toward the centre line, each leaving a motion trail of thin vertical bars behind it — purely graphic rhythm, never a data display. Spanish headings CHELSEA FC and AFC BOURNEMOUTH scale up as the blocks close in. On the final beat the blocks collide at centre and the impact flashes a lime-to-slate gradient across the seam. No numerals, no axes, no invented goals or results. Camera is a slow push toward the seam with a subtle handheld sway. Transition into the statistical variant: the impact flash wipes downward and resolves into a single bar. Statistical variant — one horizontal stacked bar. Chart type: a single stacked bar representing the whole history of meetings, split into three segments read left to right: Victorias Chelsea FC in lime #c5ed74, Empates in warm white, Victorias AFC Bournemouth in slate #8ca6bf, all sharing one scale that runs from zero to {{h2h.total}} partidos so the segments sum to the full bar. Spanish unit label: partidos. Segment values resolved from {{h2h.homeWins}}, {{h2h.draws}} and {{h2h.awayWins}}. A total marker above the bar reads Cruces previos with the value from {{h2h.total}}, and the sample annotation muestra: {{h2h.total}} cruces sits beneath it; source credit Bzzoiro in small warm white type at the foot. A persistent Spanish footnote reads historial, no pronóstico so the history is never read as a forecast. Entry: the bar draws from the left edge, segments filling in order while their numerals count up. Emphasis: a lime outline closes around the largest segment and the remaining segments drop to subdued tone. Camera pulls back to centre the full bar. Exit: the three segments separate slightly, fade in sequence, and the frame dissolves to charcoal.
